h1: Seasonal Allergies in Texas and How to Deal with Them

blocks.alt: Seasonal Allergies in Texas and How to Deal with Them

blocks.html: If you’re someone who suffers from allergies, you’ll be familiar with the puffy eyes, runny nose, and red rashes that often accompany them. Allergies are no fun, but they’re a very common condition. In fact, it’s estimated that over 50 million Americans suffer from them in some one form or another each and every year.

For many, allergies represent an annoying yet inevitable part of life. In the state of Texas, those with allergies tend to suffer quite a bit. Each season brings something new to torment the ears, eyes, and noses of Texas residents.
Seasonal allergies in Texas are no joke, but there are things you can do to handle them a little bit better.

Spring is the season when new oak trees begin to grow. This, of course, produces pollen, which spells trouble for allergy sufferers. Other culprits such as cottonwood, elm, ash, and can add to the allergens in the air at this time.

There are several types of grass found in Texas that produce allergens in summer. Some of these include Bahia, Bermuda, Orchard, Sweet Vernal, and Timothy Grass. These can be found anywhere, from the side of the road to the banks of a river.

The ragweed plant is the worst offender when it comes to allergen spreaders in the fall. In certain parts of Texas, this plant tends to grow freely which can make it particularly potent. These super-spreaders can emit as much as one billion grains of pollen in one season.

Winter is arguably the worst time of year to be in Texas if you suffer from allergies. This is owing to the propagation of the cedar tree. This tree is found all throughout the state, and many people develop reactions so severe they feel as though they’ve got a case of the flu.

blocks.text: Dealing With Seasonal Allergies in Texas

blocks.html: There’s no doubt it’s tough to be in Texas if you’re prone to allergies, but there are some things you can do.
First, you should try to take over-the-counter medications or antihistamines whenever you feel allergy symptoms. These can be quite effective for many people.

Other than this, you can try replacing the carpet in your home with wooden floors, these are easier to clean and harbor less pollen. Similarly, a leather or vinyl sofa will work much better than a fabric one.
If none of this is helpful, there are several places that offer allergy services and solutions to deal with your symptoms.
